author: opus
original:
30 mpg (US) is about **7.8 L/100 km**.

**Working:**
- 1 US gallon = 3.785 L; 1 mile = 1.609 km
- 30 miles = 48.28 km, so the car travels 48.28 km on 3.785 L, or 12.75 km per litre
- 100 km ÷ 12.75 km/L ≈ **7.84 L**

**Shortcut:** L/100 km ≈ 235.2 ÷ mpg (US). So 235.2 ÷ 30 ≈ 7.84.

US test figures (EPA) can differ from Australian ratings, so real-world comparisons may vary somewhat.
text:
To answer your question, 30 miles per gallon (US) works out to about **7.8 L/100 km**.

**Working:**
- To begin, recall the two conversion factors needed: 1 US gallon = 3.785 L, and 1 mile = 1.609 km.
- Applying the mile conversion, 30 miles = 48.28 km. This means the car travels 48.28 km on 3.785 L, or 12.75 km per litre.
- Finally, 100 km ÷ 12.75 km/L ≈ **7.84 L**, which matches the figure given above.

**Shortcut:** There is also a quicker route to the same result. L/100 km ≈ 235.2 ÷ mpg (US). So, for this car, 235.2 ÷ 30 ≈ 7.84.

I hope this helps. Please note that US test figures (EPA) can differ from Australian ratings, so real-world comparisons may vary somewhat.
